[USER] User inquired about common rituals associated with the Jewish holiday of Passover and their symbolism.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Seder is a ritual feast that takes place on the first two nights of Passover, involving the retelling of the story of the Exodus.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Matzah is a type of unleavened bread eaten during Passover, representing the haste of the Jews leaving Egypt.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Seder involves drinking four cups of wine, representing the four promises made by God to Moses in Exodus 6:6-7.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Bitter herbs, such as horseradish, symbolize the bitterness of slavery during the Seder.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] A hard-boiled egg on the Seder plate represents rebirth and renewal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Charoset, a sweet mixture of apples, nuts, and wine, represents the mortar used by Jewish slaves in Egypt.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] An empty cup for the prophet Elijah is placed on the table during the Seder.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] These rituals remind Jews of their heritage and their ancestors' struggle for freedom from slavery.  
[USER] User asked about the significance of the number four in Passover rituals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The number four represents the four promises made by God to Moses in Exodus 6:6-7, corresponding to the four cups of wine.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Each promise is represented by one of the cups of wine during the Seder.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The number four also represents the four matriarchs of the Jewish people and the four corners of the Earth.  
[USER] User inquired if all Jewish families celebrate Passover in the same way or if there are variations in rituals and traditions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There are shared traditions and rituals, but variations exist between different Jewish families and communities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Variations can include the order of items on the Seder plate, specific songs, and prayers.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Different Jewish communities may have unique regional dishes or customs associated with Passover.  
[USER] User asked why it is important to use matzah instead of regular bread during Passover.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Matzah reflects the hurried exit of the Jewish people from Egypt, as they did not have time to let their bread rise.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Matzah must adhere to specific preparation rules, using only flour and water
